summary: This script starts a headless Chrome browser in the background with remote debugging enabled, captures its process ID, runs a Behat test suite against it, and then cleans up by killing the Chrome process when done.

explanations.3: Clears the terminal screen to start with a clean display.
explanations.8: nohup runs the command immune to hangups so Chrome keeps running even if the script's terminal closes; the backslash at the end continues the command on the next line.
explanations.10: Redirects all output to /dev/null (discarding it), and the & at the end runs Chrome in the background so the script doesn't wait for it to finish.
explanations.13: $! is a special variable that holds the process ID of the last background command, so we can refer to Chrome later.
explanations.15: This tells the shell linter to ignore warnings about unquoted variables on the next line — we're intentionally using them unquoted here.
explanations.16: Sets PHP's memory limit to unlimited (-1) and then runs Behat, which is a testing framework that will execute automated tests.
explanations.18: Checks if chromePID is greater than 0, meaning Chrome was actually started successfully.
